animation.notes: Frames are written by FiestaBoard one at a time (transition plugins step frame-by-frame); the board's own flap cascade animates each write. ~1 frame/s is the practical ceiling for legible flap motion on the local API. Cloud connections are additionally floored by FiestaBoard at one write per 15 s (transport policy, not device capability).

animation.notes: Verified on a Pixoo 64 (hardware 92) on 2026-10-04, camera-timed. FiestaBoard SNAPS on this device: maxFps 2 is the verified safe still-push rate, below every LED transition's minimum, so the resolved transition is none and preview and device both cut. Why not animate: Draw/SendHttpGif uploads (one POST per frame, ~190 ms each, PicNum frames, PicOffset index, PicSpeed ms per frame, PicData base64 RGB888 row-major from the top left, PicWidth 64) LOOP FOREVER with no play-once flag; any upload longer than ~1.2 s (more than ~3 frames) shows a LOADING overlay from ~1.5 s after the first POST until ~0.5 s after the last (8 frames 1.3 s, 32 frames 4.8 s, 40 frames 6.3 s); landing on a still after an animation keeps the old loop running with frame 0 replaced for ~5 s. A single-frame push shows in ~0.5 s with no overlay. Frame cap: 59 frames were accepted but playback wrapped at ~55 (frames 55+ silently dropped); 40 played completely, so an explicit multi-frame upload should stay at 40 frames or fewer. Push spacing: 20 single-frame pushes at 1.0 s and 0.5 s all displayed in order. PicID: an upload displays only if PicID > the last accepted one (skipping ahead is fine); a reused or lower PicID still answers error_code 0 but is silently ignored, so error_code 0 means accepted, not shown. Draw/GetHttpGifId returns the next id (0 right after a reset). Draw/ResetHttpGifId does not clear the screen and needs no wait afterwards. Not verified: the community report of a freeze after ~300 pushes without a reset (the lab stayed under 25 ids between resets), and behaviour on other firmware. mDNS: the device advertises nothing.
sources: FiestaBoard hardware lab on a Pixoo 64, 2026-10-04 (camera-timed; fiestaboard-output--divoom-pixoo PR #1)
https://doc.divoom-gz.com/web/#/12?page_id=93 (Draw/SendHttpGif; read via the ShowDoc JSON API)

animation.notes: Custom apps take `draw` ops (dp/dl/dr/df/dc/dfc/dt/db) over HTTP or MQTT; `db` with a full 8×32 bitmap returned ErrorParsingJson (#214). TSPEED (app transition) defaults to 500 ms, ATIME 7 s. No stated rate limit; the push rate is UNMEASURED (no test device), so the model is held at a nominal 2 fps — below every animated entry's minimum — and stays on snap, letting the firmware's own Slide transition carry the change.

DDP on UDP 4048 (480 RGB pixels per 1440-byte datagram; 1024 LEDs = 3 datagrams a frame) holds 25–40 fps on an ESP32; E1.31 is documented at '25 ms (40 fps)' for ≤ 510 LEDs; WLED_FPS default 42. The JSON `seg.i` route is HTTP + parse per call and not for this.
rpi-rgb-led-matrix refreshes 'typically in the hundreds of Hertz' (three 128×64 panels: 410 Hz); a Pi daemon fed over the network (flaschen-taschen style) holds 30–60 fps.
As hub75_64x32; a 128×64 chain still refreshes above 100 Hz on a Pi 4.

A 32×8 frame is 32 bytes over SPI; MD_Parola's setSpeed() runs animations at any ms interval ('zero to run as fast as possible'). Hundreds of fps locally (unverified figure); the bridge from a host to the module is custom, so the figure assumes you own it.
HUB12 modules are scanned by the host microcontroller (DMD32 / DMD_STM32, 30–70 µs row on-time); a frame over serial is 64 bytes. No standard host protocol, so the figure assumes you own the bridge.

Tronbyt server: POST /v0/devices/{id}/push with a base64 WebP, displayTimeSec default 30; devices poll /next and loop the animation. Pixlet render.Root(delay=ms) sets the frame time (50 ms default — unverified). Tidbyt's cloud is rate-limited with no published number. One WebP per message change, so a flip is a sequence at 80 ms per step with no half-flaps.
